author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected on a page prefilled with its current values. A valid correction updates that visit in place and returns to the owner's record; an invalid one is refused under the booking rules.
acceptance_criteria: [REQ-VIS-003] given a booked visit, when its correction page is opened, then the page shows that visit's current date and description.
[REQ-VIS-003] given a booked visit, when a description and a date later than today are supplied, then that visit is updated, the pet gains no further visit, and the owner's record is shown.
[REQ-VIS-003] given a blank description, when the correction is submitted, then the correction is refused, the description is named, and the visit is unchanged.
[REQ-VIS-003] given a date of today or earlier, when the correction is submitted, then the correction is refused, the date is named, and the visit is unchanged.
[REQ-VIS-003] Edge case 3: correcting a visit that does not exist, or that does not belong to the named pet and owner, is refused, and no visit changes.
non_goals: Any link or button to the correction page on the owner detail page or elsewhere; the page is reachable by its URL alone (owner decision, intake line 1)
Correcting anything other than the visit's date and description (e.g. moving a visit to another pet)
Relaxing the future-date rule for corrections of past visits (recorded as an open question in docs/prd.md)
notes: Owner-specified surface from the intake request (context for design, not PRD content): GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit; reuse template pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm and its `visit` model attribute; on success redirect to the owner detail page; on validation failure redisplay the form. Edge case 3 is my reversible decision mirroring Visits edge case 1 (booking against a pet of another owner is refused); how the refusal is presented is a design choice. Open questions recorded in docs/prd.md Open Questions: correcting past-dated visits, and a visible entry point. Durable-memory changes this dispatch: docs/prd.md (NG-5 row, preamble, Visits narrative, Done-when, edge case 3, open questions), new docs/adr/2026-09-18-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md, status line of docs/adr/2026-08-08-non-goal-deletion-and-visit-amendment.md. docs/adr/README.md index needs a row for the new ADR; that file is outside my write scope. No autofix records to audit. No new ubiquitous-language terms resolved.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Visit correction reuses the pet-edit shape PetController already demonstrates (optional path variable selects new-versus-existing in the @ModelAttribute method; GET renders the shared form; POST validates, saves through OwnerRepository, redirects to /owners/{ownerId}). One adjustment: VisitController.loadPetWithVisit creates and appends a fresh Visit to the pet on every request, so on the edit routes it must instead resolve the pet's existing visit by visitId. Otherwise the save would cascade a second visit. The lookup goes through the aggregate (Owner.getPet(Integer) then a new Pet lookup of a visit by id, mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer)), per system-design.md § Contracts invariants (Owner is the entry point; no VisitRepository). NG-5 is narrowed by the recorded owner decision (intake line 1, docs/adr/2026-09-18-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md), so there is no conflict. Basis: grep and read of VisitController, PetController, Owner, Pet, Visit (IDE oracle not connected; weaker basis).
integration_points: Entry point GET/POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit binds into the persisted Visit resolved through Owner -> Pet -> visit id, behind an allow-list: the `visit` binder admits only date and description and keeps id and *.id disallowed (security-principles.md § mass assignment row; system-design.md Threat Model mass-assignment row). The same binder serves booking, whose form offers only those two fields, so booking behavior is unchanged.

The edit POST must not request-bind Owner: take the owner from the model with binding disabled (@ModelAttribute(name = "owner", binding = false)) and save it through OwnerRepository, the sole write path (system-design.md § Contracts, OwnerRepository row).

Validation mirrors booking: @Valid Visit (description @NotBlank) plus the not-after-today rejection with error code typeMismatch.visitDate on date. Sharing that check between the two POST handlers is a TDD Refactor step, not a precondition.

Template: pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm needs no change. The form has no th:action, so it posts back to the edit URL; the heading drops 'New' through visit['new']. If the button label is changed for the edit case, it must come from a message key present in every bundle (REQ-LANG-002). A hard-coded literal like the pet form's is not allowed.

Double for the repository boundary: keep the existing @MockitoBean OwnerRepository in the @WebMvcTest, and stub only findById to return a real Owner -> Pet -> Visit graph with ids set. This is a conscious framework-stub exception (testing-principles.md § Mocking Policy): a hand-written double of a Spring Data JpaRepository has too wide a surface, and a real repository would change the test slice. Assert on the real in-memory graph: the visit's date and description are changed or unchanged, and pet.getVisits() size is unchanged. Do not assert on stub interactions for these outcomes.
Transport: MockMvc, the sanctioned harness (CLAUDE.md § Testing Strategy).

patterns.description: findPet: @ModelAttribute method branching on an optional path variable between a new and an existing aggregate member
initUpdateForm / processUpdateForm: edit GET and POST on the shared create-or-update template, redirecting to redirect:/owners/{ownerId}
getPet(Integer): identity lookup inside the aggregate; Pet gains the same shape for its visits

risks.risk: The controller-wide loadPetWithVisit appends a new transient Visit on the edit routes too. Saving the owner would then cascade an extra visit (breaching 'the pet gains no further visit') or fail @NotBlank on persist.
risks.mitigation: Branch the @ModelAttribute("visit") method on an optional visitId path variable, as PetController.findPet does: create and append only when visitId is absent. System-design.md § Contracts, VisitController row: 'updates the pet's existing visit in place'.

risks.risk: Edge case 3: a visitId that is absent from the named pet, or a pet absent from the named owner, could be edited if looked up by visit id alone.
risks.mitigation: Resolve only through Owner.getPet(petId) and then the pet's own visits. When either is missing, refuse the same way the existing owner-not-found and pet-not-found paths do (IllegalArgumentException from the model-attribute method), before any binding or save. System-design.md § Contracts invariant: 'reached for correction through its owner and then its pet'.

risks.risk: A refused correction leaves the detached in-memory visit mutated by binding.
risks.mitigation: No save on the error path. open-in-view is off and the controller runs no transaction (system-design.md § Persistence), so the stored visit is unchanged. Tests assert this through the real graph: the stub returns a fresh graph per test.

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records; skipped. Durable-memory writes: docs/system-design.md adds REQ-VIS-003 to the Pet, Visit, OwnerRepository and VisitController Contracts rows and a purpose clause on Pet and VisitController, adds a correction-reach invariant to 'Invariants the rows cannot carry', and extends the Threat Model mass-assignment row with the visit binder allow-list. docs/adr/README.md adds the index row for the 2026-09-18 non-goal ADR and marks the 2026-08-08 row's status as NG-5 narrowed. No new architectural ADR: the edit mechanism is contained in this slice. Non-goal ADR edits (both files) are the product-requirements-expert's and are recorded in its prd-entry (line 3). Open questions (narrowest reading taken, not blocking): (1) edge case 3 is presented through the existing exception/error-page refusal, not a 404; whether not-found refusals should become 404s is project-wide and out of scope. (2) Observation, not verified by test: processNewVisitForm request-binds @ModelAttribute Owner behind only the id disallow list. The allow-list on the `visit` binder does not cover the `owner` attribute, so booking may still bind owner fields. This is pre-existing and outside this slice; it is a candidate Known Defect for a human to confirm.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Mass assignment closed on the edit path: VisitController.java:58-61 `@InitBinder("visit")` sets `setAllowedFields("date", "description")` on top of the class-wide `setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id")` (line 55), and processUpdateVisitForm binds the owner with `@ModelAttribute(name = "owner", binding = false)` (line 141), so only date and description reach the saved graph. The template's hidden `petId` input cannot rebind anything. The allow-list also narrows the existing booking path, which is a stricter control and not a weakened one.

Ownership is enforced server-side on every request: loadPetWithVisit resolves owner -> pet -> visit through `pet.getVisit(visitId)` (Pet.java getVisit iterates only this pet's persisted visits), so a visit id belonging to another pet or owner is refused before binding. The parameterized test covers the other-pet, unknown-visit, and unknown-pet cases, and asserts that nothing is saved.

The edit path runs the same controls as booking: `@Valid Visit` (NotBlank description) plus the shared rejectNonFutureDate helper, which the create path also uses now, so both persisting paths validate the same way.

Error text follows the existing pattern: the new IllegalArgumentException message (VisitController.java:96) carries only numeric path ids, which the request already contains. It carries no credential or internal detail, as docs/security-principles.md line 37 requires.

Output escaping holds: createOrUpdateVisitForm.html renders visit data only through th:text (lines 52-53). `grep -rn -F -e utext -e '__${' src/main/resources/templates` returned no hits. The template changed in no way (git status shows no src/main/resources changes).
No data access changes, no string-built queries, and no secrets appear in the diff. Checked by reading the full src diff via scripts/changeset.py.

Supply chain: build.gradle is not in the change set. The resolved runtime classpath shows spring-webmvc 7.0.9 and jackson-databind 3.1.5 (./gradlew dependencies). dependencyCheckAnalyze is not configured (no match for dependencyCheck in build.gradle), so no NVD match ran in this review.

author: change-grader
summary: add in-place correction of a booked visit

blast_radius.note: Two production files in the owner package (VisitController, Pet) plus a consistent doc set that narrows NG-5 per the recorded owner decision; no sensitive paths, no schema, template or build change. The new POST route is a write on the declared security surface, but the threat model already lists the owner and pet edit routes under the same unauthenticated posture, so the reach matches existing flows.

semantic_surprise.note: Read every prod hunk: the extracted rejectNonFutureDate keeps the original !isAfter(now) boundary, the optional visitId path variable is null on the /new routes so booking still appends a fresh visit, and the edit lookup goes owner then pet then Pet.getVisit, which skips unsaved visits. With open-in-view=false and EAGER cascade mappings, the owner is detached, so a refused correction never saves, and a valid save merges the existing visit id in place. The one behavior change outside the new route is that the visit allow-list (date, description) also narrows booking binding; the design-block recorded that on purpose and it is stricter.

test_adequacy.note: Controller tests assert real outcomes: recursive comparison of the corrected visit, containsExactly on the pet's visits (no second visit), save called or never called, field-error codes, and a parameterized refusal for an unknown visit, another pet's visit and an unknown pet that checks both visits stay unchanged. PetTests unit-tests getVisit's match, miss and isNew guard. The residual gap is that in-place persistence is proven against a mocked repository, not through a real JPA merge, the same level the existing booking tests use.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four reviewers approved with no findings or recommendations. The only round-1 block (test-reviewer, missing Pet.getVisit unit test) was fixed in a test-only delta and re-approved. Spot-checked citations resolve (VisitController.java:45, :96, :141). The unconfigured dependencyCheck is a standing project gap, not a hedge.

scope_deviation.note: Zero build retries, consultations and design revisions. The diff delivers exactly the requested GET/POST edit route, reuses the existing template, adds no owner-page link as the owner decided, records the NG-5 narrowing in a new non-goal ADR, and lists both open questions (correcting past-dated visits, a future entry-point link) in the PRD instead of settling them.

rationale: Contained, well-tested correction route that follows the existing pet-edit shape. Every prod hunk reads as intended, and the refusal paths neither save nor leak across owners. A glance is enough. Note the recorded product consequence: a correction must carry a future date, so a past visit's description cannot be fixed without moving its date.
